evidence: As logged-in seller (Emma Green), created a new listing "Upcycled Glass Bottle Lamp" with a photo, description, price ($40), category (Home Decor), condition (Good), and location (Brooklyn, NY). Submission succeeded with toast "Listing created successfully!" and the new listing appears in My Listings with correct title, price, description, and Active status.

actual: In My Listings, each listing only offers "View", "Mark Sold", and "Delete" actions; there is no Edit control. Clicking the listing title or image does nothing (no navigation). Directly navigating to a guessed edit route (/edit-listing/:id) returns a 404. Sellers have no way to update an existing listing's details (title, description, price, category, condition, location).
Same as FT-2: My Listings page provides no Edit action, only View/Mark Sold/Delete. There is no UI path for a seller to update information on a product they own.

issue: Update feature does not exist, so the restriction cannot be verified
actual: Since no listing-update feature exists at all in the UI (only View/Mark Sold/Delete, and the guessed edit route 404s), it is impossible to verify that sellers are blocked from updating other sellers' listings; the underlying capability being restricted is entirely absent.

evidence: Submitted the Create Listing form with all fields empty. Form did not submit (remained on /create-listing, no success toast), and focus moved to the required Title field indicating browser-enforced required-field validation.

Filled the listing form with Price = -25 and all other required fields, then submitted. Form did not submit (remained on /create-listing, no success toast) and focus returned to the Price field, indicating the negative price was rejected by validation.
Typed "Denim" into the search box; results filtered from 10 items to 1 item, showing only "Vintage Denim Jacket - Size M", confirming keyword search works.
Search results updated instantly to show "1 items available" as soon as "Denim" was typed into the search box, with no submit button or page reload required.

Verified category filter (Furniture -> 3 items), condition filter (Fair -> 1 item: Kids Wooden Train Set), sort by "Price: Low to High" (list reordered ascending $35→$320), and the Price Range slider (dragging min updated displayed range "$0-$500" to "$10-$500" and re-filtered results). Category, condition, price range, and sort/distance controls all function as buyer filtering/sorting tools.

Toggling category checkbox (Furniture) and condition checkbox (Fair) immediately updated the "N items available" count and the visible product list without any submit action or page reload, confirming real-time filtering.
On /product/prod-4, clicked "Add to Cart" (e3055). Header cart icon button changed from icon-only to "1" badge, confirming item was added to cart.

Immediately after clicking "Add to Cart", a toast notification "Added to cart!" appeared in the Notifications region, and the cart icon badge updated to "1" in the header, providing clear visual feedback.

On /cart with 1 item, clicked "Send Purchase Request" (e3108). Toast "Purchase requests sent to sellers!" appeared, and cart cleared to "0 items" / "Your cart is empty", confirming the purchase request was submitted successfully.

issue: No verifiable mechanism removes only unavailable/sold items from an existing cart
actual: As Emma, added two items to cart from different sellers (Kids Wooden Train Set/Sofia and Harry Potter Book Set/Marcus), confirmed cart badge showed "2". Logged in as Sofia and marked the Kids Wooden Train Set "Sold" (confirmed via My Listings status change and it disappearing from the public Browse grid, 10->9 items). Logged back in as Emma to check the cart: it showed "0 items"/"Your cart is empty" - i.e. BOTH the now-sold item and the still-active Harry Potter book were wiped, not just the unavailable one. This indicates the cart is indiscriminately cleared on logout/login rather than being selectively filtered based on listing availability; no distinct feature was found that flags/removes only unavailable items while preserving valid cart items during a session.

evidence: Inspected img alt/src attributes for all 10 browse-page listings via DOM query. Each product has a unique, distinct Unsplash photo URL whose alt text matches its listing title, and each image is thematically appropriate to the described item (e.g., "Reclaimed Wood Bookshelf" -> distinct bookshelf photo, "Sony Noise-Canceling Headphones" -> distinct headphones photo, "Vintage Denim Jacket - Size M" -> distinct jacket photo, "Complete Harry Potter Book Set" -> distinct books photo). No generic/mismatched placeholder images were found across the sampled listings.
